items.title: 2D Pen Plotter Robot
items.description: Custom hardware automated writing robot built from scratch using CNC techniques, stepper drivers, and G-code interpretation.
items.problem: Writing repetitive documents by hand wastes hours and off-the-shelf plotters are expensive.
items.solution: Designed a 2-axis CNC plotter driven by an Arduino: custom G-code parser, stepper control with A4988 drivers, and a pen lift servo.
items.challenges: Backlash in the belt drive and timing jitter in step pulses; solved with acceleration profiles and interrupt-driven stepping.
items.results: Repeatable sub-millimetre accuracy on A4 paper at a fraction of commercial cost.
items.impact: Became my gateway into embedded control loops and motion systems.

items.title: Line Follower Robot
items.description: Autonomous PID-controlled robot navigating complex tracks using IR sensor arrays and real-time motor tuning.
items.problem: Naive on/off steering makes line followers oscillate and lose the track on sharp curves.
items.solution: Implemented a tuned PID loop over an 8-sensor IR array with weighted position estimation and dynamic speed scaling.
items.challenges: Sensor calibration under changing ambient light; added auto-calibration sweep at startup.
items.results: Stable high-speed runs through intersections, gaps, and hairpin turns.
items.impact: Competition-ready platform reused by juniors as a learning base.

items.title: Competitive Programming Library
items.description: Battle-tested C++ templates for graphs, number theory, DP optimizations, and data structures used in live contests.
items.problem: Re-deriving standard algorithms under contest pressure costs precious minutes.
items.solution: Curated a personal library of tested, benchmarked snippets: segment trees, LIS, Dijkstra, modular arithmetic, and more.
items.challenges: Balancing genericity with contest-speed typing; settled on short, memorizable implementations.
items.results: Consistently faster problem-to-AC time in rated contests.
items.impact: Shared with my university's CP community.

items.title: Cinematic Campus Aftermovie
items.description: Shot and edited a high-energy event aftermovie with color grading, sound design, and motion graphics.
items.problem: Event recaps are usually long, flat, and unwatched.
items.solution: A tight edit: beat-matched cuts, speed ramps, clean sound design, and a consistent color grade.
items.challenges: Mixed footage sources with different color profiles; normalized via LUT pipeline.
items.results: A tight aftermovie that the audience actually rewatched and shared.
items.impact: Set the visual standard for subsequent campus events.

items.title: Algorithms in Competitive Programming
items.description: Campus presentation on optimization techniques and dynamic programming — from brute force to O(n log n) elegance.
